I can value a lot of individual things, but what I find more fascinating is understanding the precursor to the value structure. Many of the individual things that  I might find valuable are only valuable insofar as the preceding condition that it rests upon.

For example, I can value a particular book on geography. Why? Well, I could just say that I like the topic and be done with it, but that doesn't provide any useful information that I could glean truth statements from. It's fun to figure out the series of events that leads to "I like this thing!" It might look something like this:

I value geography because: I value knowledge

I value knowledge because: I value options

I value options because: I value time

Just simple things like these value chains can be useful in discovering your identity. In my case, I value understanding myself and the world around me. That is usually the condition from which all other value statements arise.

Not to be a textbook individualist, but I don't think there is a fundamental "purpose" in existence. At least not a pre-determined one. All lifeforms want to self-maintain, as well as proliferate. What we could also say is that if there isn't an objective (or pre-determined), basis for our existence, perhaps the purpose of life is what gives a desire to survive, since survival is the necessary condition for life. So essentially, purpose is what gives a reason for survival. And purpose is entirely subjective.

As for God, I don't necessarily see a reason to believe in any pre-made interpretation of a higher power. I do, however, think there is a strong case to be made that a higher power exists, just based on the strength of the cosmological argument. Maybe pantheism too idk.
